q: Traffic receipts: keep in the order of occurrence- a) Posting on the Receipts side of Cashier's cash book b) Posting in Traffic Check sheet c) Preparation of CR/TR note and MCRs d) Posting in the General Cash Book & AO sign as a token of reconciliation daily on Cashier's cash Book
e: The correct answer is c, a, b, d. The correct option is (B): the correct order is c, a, b, d. First the CR/TR note is prepared with MCRs (the station's remittance document), then it is posted on the receipts side of the Cashier's Cash Book, then in the Traffic Check Sheet, and finally in the General Cash Book with the AO's daily signature as token of reconciliation. Each step builds on the previous document. Related exam fact: the traffic check sheet is a subsidiary record — station remittances never go straight to the journal.

q: The check exercised by railway accounts office on financial transactions is called
e: Internal Check — that is the right answer. The correct option is (C) Internal Check. The check exercised by the railway accounts office on financial transactions — verifying vouchers, sanctions and classifications in the course of accounting — is called internal check. It is a concurrent, built-in control of the accounting process itself. Related exam fact: internal check (concurrent control by accounts) is different from internal audit (independent appraisal) and from the C&AG's statutory audit.

q: Independent appraisal function of review of selected activities by Accounts team is called
e: Internal Audit — that is the right answer. The correct option is (D) Internal Audit. The independent appraisal function — review of selected activities by the accounts team acting independently of the accounting process — is called internal audit. Unlike internal check, it is not part of day-to-day accounting but a separate evaluative review. Related exam fact: internal audit is distinct from the C&AG's external statutory audit and is also not one of the three purposes of railway audit (accountancy, appropriation, administrative).

q: Name the supreme statutory Audit Organisation in India
e: The correct option is (A) C&AG. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is the supreme statutory audit organisation in the country, auditing government and railway accounts under constitutional authority. Appropriation is Parliament's authorisation, through the Appropriation Act, to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund for the voted demands. q: Audit objections raised on Accounts as a result of voucher check are called
e: Option C (Audit note) is the correct choice. The correct option is (C) Audit note. Audit objections raised on accounts as a result of voucher check are called audit notes — the first formal written objection from audit on the accounts. Unsettled audit notes can escalate into draft paras and eventually audit paras in the C&AG's report. Related exam fact: an Audit Inspection Report is the broader inspection document, while a special letter is used for important matters needing higher attention.
